gallery.text:
BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just dropped Claude Fable 5.2. It’s a paradigm-shifting model if you have a project ambitious enough to give it.

We’ve been testing it at @every, and I’ve seen this crazy explosion of creativity on the team. People are making their own creative software, games for their kids, and documentaries instead of slide decks.

Here’s your day zero vibe check:

• Coding: @kieranklaassen built Everycut, a video editor with the features we use from Premiere, Descript, and other tools—all in one app, with an agent built in. The first version was live in 3 days, and we immediately used it for our internal show-and-tell. This feels like a new era of professionals building their own professional tools, tailored to exactly how they work.

• Games and design: @jackcheng gave it a photo of his toddler’s messy playroom. It turned the actual toys into a playable racing game, with fun details like a stray shoe as an obstacle and a sippy cup as a power-up.

• Knowledge work: @hammer_mt turned his research into a documentary. The model came up with interview questions, he answered them on camera, and it cut the footage together. He called this the most productive 3 weeks of his career.

• A different way of working: Give it a big job and leave it running overnight or over a weekend. But tell it what “done” means: Mike found it could finish the build, then spend another day or two testing. Set the goal, the budget, and how much checking you need before walking away.

• The catch: It’s slow and burns through tokens. Our early-access usage was free, and these projects would have been expensive at API rates. It’s 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1, but for everyday writing, emails, or quick back-and-forth coding, I’d usually reach for something else.

The clearest signal: When our early access ended, @TylerNishida stopped working on some projects until he could get this model back. He didn’t want to build them with anything else.

The best measure of a new model is whether it makes you try things you wouldn’t have tried before.

Fable 5.2 absolutely does that.

Here’s our full day-zero Vibe Check:

gallery.text:
🚨 BREAKING: Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2 

I tested the new model and had it build a nationwide water safety map for me.

My question was which big American cities are best set up for water in the next few decades. The #1 answer, according to the model it built out, is...

Indianapolis, Indiana.

From one prompt, it scoured federal data across the EPA, USGS, NOAA, FEMA, and the Census Bureau (more than 5 GB, including 15.5 million EPA violation records and 2 million PFAS test results). Then I had a dozen other AI agents check its work (which found some errors, like Alaska’s North Slope getting a high score because its temperature data was missing).

The final map rates 3,100 counties and more than 900 city areas on 17 measures. On an aggregate score between water supply, climate outlook, water quality, testing and oversight, and backup, Indianapolis scored the highest. Cleveland trails by about a tenth of a point, with Cincinnati, St. Louis, and Nashville right behind.
It is insane to me that I can have a research question in my head and get this level of insight hours later.

The new model also built out this trailer video below.

你负责这个 repo，然后你需要把我的这个 character creator 从一个游戏的模型弄成一个世界顶尖的数字人类模型。

build a fully animated 3d raccoon on rollerblades, with Fable 5.2 + Blender…

the skating feels natural because every movement follows the character’s weight

here’s the workflow:

> step 1: block out the raccoon with simple shapes, keeping the proportions and silhouette readable
> step 2: build the fur, striped tail, paws and facial details
> step 3: model the rollerblades with separate wheels, frames and straps
> step 4: add the orange protective gear, with layered materials and surface details
> step 5: create the skeleton and rig the legs, arms, spine and tail
> step 6: set up the skating cycle with alternating pushes, gliding and weight shifts
> step 7: animate the tail and upper body to balance each movement
> step 8: refine the timing with animation curves, keeping the wheels aligned with the ground
> step 9: add lighting, materials and a final render pass, then test the animation for sliding and clipping

who does what:

fable 5.2: character design and visual direction
blender: the model, the rig, the animation
animation curves: the timing, the balance, the transitions
you: the creative direction

less random movement, more controlled weight. good animation comes from how every small motion supports the next

- 输入：$8 / 百万 Token
- 输出：$40 / 百万 Token

另外还提供 Fast Mode，最高提速 2.5 倍。

两者实际上是同一个底层模型。Fable 配备更严格的网络安全和生物安全防护，面向普通用户；Mythos 则面向经过审核的网络安全和生命科学研究机构。
